title: Pub Astrophysics
desc: Quantum weirdness, medical myths debunked & numbers that break your brain

questions.q: The observable universe is 13.8 billion years old — but its radius is 46 billion light-years. How is that possible?
questions.a: Space itself has been expanding faster than light — the light we see left objects that have since moved much farther away

questions.q: What is the Dunning-Kruger effect, and which field of science does it come from?
questions.a: A cognitive bias where low-ability people overestimate their competence — from social psychology (Kruger & Dunning, 1999)

questions.q: Absolute zero is -273.15°C. Has anything ever reached it?
questions.a: No — the Third Law of Thermodynamics says it's impossible to reach in a finite number of steps. Scientists have come within billionths of a degree

questions.q: The placebo effect works even when patients know they're taking a placebo. True or false?
questions.a: True — 'open-label placebos' have shown measurable effects in clinical trials

questions.q: Light slows down when passing through glass or water. What happens to the 'missing' speed?
questions.a: The light is absorbed and re-emitted by atoms in the medium, creating a delay — it still travels at c between atoms

questions.q: What is the Fermi Paradox, in one sentence?
questions.a: If the universe is so vast and old, why haven't we found any evidence of other intelligent civilisations?

questions.q: CRISPR gene editing was adapted from a defence mechanism found in what type of organism?
questions.a: Bacteria — they use CRISPR sequences to recognise and destroy viral DNA

questions.q: A person standing at the equator is moving faster than a fighter jet due to Earth's rotation. Roughly how fast?
questions.a: About 1,670 km/h (1,037 mph) — faster than the speed of sound

questions.q: The Mpemba effect claims hot water freezes faster than cold water. Has it been definitively proven or disproven?
questions.a: Neither — it remains contested. Some experiments confirm it, others don't. The mechanisms are still debated

questions.q: What is 'junk DNA' and why is that name now considered misleading?
questions.a: Non-coding DNA that doesn't directly make proteins — but much of it has regulatory functions, so 'junk' understates its importance
